page.title: Budgets
page.purpose: Let the operator see how much room remains under each budget and change what may be spent. Headroom is the number an operator comes here for, so it leads.

priorities.statement: Remaining headroom per budget is the first thing read, with its cap for context
A frozen budget is unmistakable and its freeze is reversible from the same place
Pending authorizations are visibly reducing headroom, not hidden until they settle
Counterparty allow and deny lists are inspectable without leaving the budget
Which budgets require human approval is visible without opening each one

states.description: Budgets exist and headroom is current.
No budget is configured; the page states what a budget does and offers to create one.
Headroom is known for some budgets and unavailable for others; the page says which rather than showing a blank.
A cap or list edit is being persisted.
A proposed cap conflicts with an existing mandate; the page names the conflict and what would resolve it.
Headroom figures are older than their refresh interval and say so.

claims.statement: Remaining headroom precedes the cap and the period in each budget's reading order.
A frozen budget is distinguishable from an exhausted one, which are different facts with different remedies.
The freeze control is separated from navigation and from non-destructive controls.
Amount columns use tabular figures so a magnitude error reads as a ragged edge.
Headroom shows the portion held by pending authorizations rather than only the settled figure.
The partial state names which budgets have unknown headroom.
